When he took his jinshi degree he had been a student of Tang Binyin, whom he had displeased; the Donglin faction in turn despised him on Binyin's account.
When he took his jinshi degree he had come from Tang Binyin's school, though Binyin did not regard him favorably; the Donglin faction nonetheless despised him on Binyin's account.
出湯賓尹之門 means he was a protégé from Tang Binyin's school; 賓尹弗善也 is Binyin not thinking well of him, not Yundeng having displeased him.

When the affair was reported, he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, given the posthumous title Zhonglie (Loyal and Fierce), granted funeral rites and sacrifice, and one son was granted enrollment in the Imperial Academy.

When the affair was reported, he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, given the posthumous title Zhonglie (Loyal and Fierce), granted funeral rites and sacrifice, and one son was granted enrollment in the Imperial Academy.
光祿寺 is the Court of Imperial Entertainments; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices is 太常寺.
When the affair was reported, Guangkui was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Guangxi and the others received posthumous honors of varying degree.
When the affair was reported, Guangkui was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Guangxi and the others received posthumous honors of varying degree.
光祿卿 heads the Court of Imperial Entertainments (光祿寺), not the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (太常寺).

That year Zijin Liang and others raided Liaozhou; Yang Yukai, a metropolitan graduate living in retirement, and Principal Secretary Zhang Youcheng assisted Prefect Li Chengzhang of Xinyang in the defense; when their strength failed and the city fell, Yukai was taken and died cursing the bandits.

That year Zijin Liang and others raided Liaozhou; Yang Yukai, a messenger living in retirement, and Principal Secretary Zhang Youcheng assisted Prefect Li Chengzhang of Xinyang in the defense; when their strength failed and the city fell, Yukai was taken and died cursing the bandits.
行人 is the office of Messenger (Messenger Office), not "metropolitan graduate".
Yukai was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Jizhong was made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
Yukai was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Jizhong was made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
光祿少卿 belongs to the Court of Imperial Entertainments (光祿寺), not the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

At the end of the Wanli reign he passed the metropolitan examination; in the second year of Tianqi he attended the palace examination and was appointed investigating censor of Chengtian Prefecture, then transferred to principal secretary in the Ministry of War.

At the end of the Wanli reign he passed the metropolitan examination; in the second year of Tianqi he attended the palace examination and was appointed judge of Chengtian Prefecture, then transferred to principal secretary in the Ministry of War.
推官 is a prefectural judge, not an investigating censor.
Junpei was known for righteous conduct; while fleeing with his son and nephew, he met bandits on the road who wished to kill his nephew.
Junpei was known for righteous conduct; while fleeing with his son and grandnephew, he met bandits on the road who wished to kill his grandnephew.
從孫 is a grandnephew (son of a nephew), not a nephew.
Vice Commissioner Zhou Shideng was at Fuzhou; the city was wholly unprepared, and the subprefect, investigating censor, and magistrate all fled.
Vice Commissioner Zhou Shideng was at Fuzhou; the city was wholly unprepared, and the assistant prefect, prefectural judge, and magistrate all fled.
通判 is an assistant prefect and 推官 a prefectural judge, not a "subprefect" and "investigating censor".
Rilin, styled Yanruo, was an enfeoffed tribute student of Poyang.
Rilin, styled Yanruo, was a tribute student by imperial grace from Poyang.
恩貢生 is a tribute student selected by imperial grace, not an "enfeoffed" tribute student.

He was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; a shrine was established, and he was worshipped together with Sicheng and Sanyuan; his wife and daughters were honored with a commemorative arch.

He was posthumously made Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; a shrine was established, and he was worshipped together with Sicheng and Sanyuan; his wife and daughters were honored with a commemorative arch.
光祿丞 is an assistant (丞) of the Court of Imperial Entertainments (光祿寺), not a "Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices".
He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
光祿少卿 belongs to the Court of Imperial Entertainments (光祿寺), not the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
Yu knew bandits would certainly come and spoke to Supervisor Lu Menglong, declining on grounds of having no troops.
Yu knew bandits would certainly come and spoke to Supervisor Lu Menglong, who declined on the grounds that he had no troops.
以無兵辭 has Lu Menglong declining for lack of troops; the translation wrongly makes Pang Yu the one declining.

Later, Supervising Secretary Lin Zhengheng memorialized the court with a full account; Meng'ao was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Shikuan Director of the same court, and the others received posthumous honors of varying degree.

Later, Supervising Secretary Lin Zhengheng memorialized the court with a full account; Meng'ao was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Shikuan Assistant Director of the same court, and the others received posthumous honors of varying degree.
光祿少卿 and 光祿丞 are the vice director and assistant director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments (光祿寺); 丞 is not "Director", and the court is not that of Imperial Sacrifices.
Qian was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the others received posthumous honors according to regulation.
Qian was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; the others received posthumous honors according to regulation.
光祿卿 heads the Court of Imperial Entertainments (光祿寺), not the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (太常寺).
He was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and a shrine was erected for his worship.
He was posthumously made Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and a shrine was erected for his worship.
光祿丞 is an assistant director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, not "Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices".
Jiyan was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the others received posthumous honors of varying degree.
Jiyan was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; the others received posthumous honors of varying degree.
光祿少卿 belongs to the Court of Imperial Entertainments (光祿寺), not the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
Administrative Aide Wan Wenying lay ill in bed; the bandits came searching for him.
Prefectural Judge Wan Wenying lay ill in bed; the bandits came searching for him.
推官 is a prefectural judge, not an "Administrative Aide".
Liang Zhiren was from Nanjing and a descendant of Marquis Ming of Baoding.
Liang Zhiren was from Nanjing and a descendant of Liang Ming, Marquis of Baoding.
保定侯銘 is Liang Ming (銘), Marquis of Baoding; "Marquis Ming" wrongly treats the personal name as part of the title.
Guoxun was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Jianzhong and the others all received posthumous honors.
Guoxun was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Jianzhong and the others all received posthumous honors.
光祿少卿 belongs to the Court of Imperial Entertainments (光祿寺), not the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
Erchun was from Shandong and was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
Erchun was from Shandong and was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
光祿少卿 belongs to the Court of Imperial Entertainments (光祿寺), not the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
Daifang was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and his wife and concubine were honored with a commemorative arch.
Daifang was posthumously made Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and his wife and concubine were honored with a commemorative arch.
光祿丞 is an assistant director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, not "Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices".
Assistant Prefect Qian Dayong died together with his wife, concubines, daughters-in-law, and sons' wives.
Assistant Prefect Qian Dayong died together with his wife, concubines, and daughters-in-law.
妻妾子婦 lists wife, concubines and daughters-in-law; the English duplicates daughters-in-law as "sons' wives".
He was transferred to investigating censor of Yingtian Prefecture and principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice, rose through posts as prefect, and returned home to mourn his parent's death.
He was transferred to judge of Yingtian Prefecture and principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice, rose through posts as prefect, and returned home to mourn his parent's death.
推官 is a prefectural judge, not an investigating censor.

The elder brother died of rage and grief; friends gathered his body for burial. Before he died he wept his full grief and said, "My younger brother died for the state; I die for my brother — can I alone fail to proclaim this deed to the world!"

The elder brother died of rage and grief; a friend gathered his body for burial, wept with the utmost grief, and said, "The younger brother died for the state and the elder brother died for his younger brother—can I alone fail to make this known!"
The subject of 哭盡哀，曰 is the friend (友人) who buried the brother, not the dead elder brother; the quotation is the friend's.
He prepared a detailed petition forcefully setting out the case, and only then was it reported to the throne.
The friend prepared a detailed petition forcefully setting out the case, and only then was it reported to the throne.
Continues the friend's action from the previous sentence; the petitioner is the friend, which the English leaves ambiguous.
Shiguang was posthumously made Recorder of Guangji, and mourning honors were granted.
Shiguang was posthumously made Registrar of Guangji, and mourning honors were granted.
主簿 is a registrar, not a recorder (典史 is the clerk/recorder post he actually held).
Before long the touring censor said that Jiazheng's filial devotion and his mother's righteousness deserved posthumous titles and hereditary honors, to uphold the moral order.
Before long the touring censor said that Jiazheng's loyalty as a son and his mother's righteousness deserved posthumous titles and hereditary honors, to uphold the moral order.
子忠母義 pairs the son's loyalty with the mother's righteousness; it is not "filial devotion".
During the Chongzhen reign he was promoted to garrison commander of the Jiangsu garrison.
During the Chongzhen reign he was promoted to garrison commander of the grand coordinator's command.
撫標守備 is a garrison commander in the grand coordinator's own command (撫標); nothing names Jiangsu.

When affairs were settled, Shangqing was posthumously made Right Assistant Censor, Shihua Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Yingqi Secretariat Associate of the Provincial Surveillance Commission, and Mengke Officer for Merit; all were granted mourning honors.

When affairs were settled, Shangqing was posthumously made Right Assistant Administration Commissioner, Shihua Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Yingqi Secretary of the Provincial Surveillance Commission, and Mengke Gentleman for Ceremonial Service; all were granted mourning honors.
右參議 is a right assistant administration commissioner, not a censor; 光祿丞 is an assistant (丞), not a vice director; 知事 is a secretary and 將仕郎 a prose rank.
Supervising Secretary Zhang Dajing came on Wencan's orders to pacify the situation, yet he too could not restrain them.
Army Supervisor and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Dajing came on Wencan's orders to pacify the situation, yet he too could not restrain them.
監軍僉事 is an army supervisor holding the rank of assistant surveillance commissioner, not a "Supervising Secretary".
Grand Coordinator Xiong Wencan agreed and settled their force of tens of thousands in the outskirts; the residents were in uproar and wished to flee.
Supreme Commander Xiong Wencan agreed and settled their force of tens of thousands in the outskirts; the residents were in uproar and wished to flee.
總理 here is Xiong Wencan's post of supreme commander over the bandit-suppression armies, not a grand coordinator (巡撫).
In the twelfth year he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Huguang and supervised the armies of Yun and Xiang.
In the twelfth year he was promoted to Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang and supervised the armies of Yun and Xiang.
僉事 is an assistant surveillance commissioner, not a vice commissioner.
His merit in defeating bandits was recorded; he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor while continuing to supervise troops as before.
His merit in defeating bandits was recorded; he was promoted to Right Assistant Administration Commissioner while continuing to supervise troops as before.
右參議 is a right assistant administration commissioner, not a censor.
Push Official Kuang Yueguang, Acting County Administrator Li Dajue, and Mobile Battalion Commander Li Min'an also died in the affair.
Prefectural Judge Kuang Yueguang, Acting County Administrator Li Dajue, and Mobile Corps Commander Li Min'an also died in the affair.
推官 is a prefectural judge; "Push Official" is a literal calque.
He was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, presented eleven points on the advantages and disadvantages of white-grain transport, and all were approved and carried out.

He was transferred to Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, presented eleven points on the advantages and disadvantages of white-grain transport, and all were approved and carried out.
光祿丞 is an assistant director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, not "Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices".

Later the emperor summoned Grand Secretary He Fengsheng and had him fully recount the circumstances of his death in service; the posthumous rank was changed to Vice Minister of the Directorate of Horses.

Later the emperor summoned Grand Secretary He Fengsheng and had him fully recount the circumstances of his death in service; the posthumous rank was changed to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
太仆少卿 is the vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud (太僕寺), not a "Directorate of Horses".
Suizhou had fallen in the first month of the tenth year; it fell again on this occasion, and fell once more in the seventh month; Judge Yu Qian died there.
Suizhou had fallen in the first month of the tenth year; it fell again on this occasion, and fell once more in the seventh month; Sub-prefectural Judge Yu Que died there.
塙 reads què, so 余塙 is Yu Que; 判官 is a sub-prefectural judge.
